29.0.0.en: 1 Woe to Ariel, to Ariel, the city where David dwelt! add ye year to year; let the feasts go round. 2 Yet I will distress Ariel, and there shall be heaviness and sorrow: and it shall be unto me as Ariel. 3 And I will camp against thee round about, and will lay siege against thee with a mount, and I will raise forts against thee. 4 And thou shalt be brought down, and shalt speak out of the ground, and thy speech shall be low out of the dust, and thy voice shall be as a phantom out of the ground, and thy speech shall whisper out of the dust. 5 Moreover the multitude of thine enemies shall be like small dust, and the multitude of the terrible ones shall be as chaff that passeth away: yea, it shall be at an instant suddenly. 6 Thou shalt be visited of the LORD of hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire. 7 And the multitude of all the nations that fight against Ariel, even all that fight against her and her munition, and that distress her, shall be as a dream of a night vision. 8 It shall even be as when an hungry man dreameth, and, behold, he eateth; but he awaketh, and his soul is empty: or as when a thirsty man dreameth, and, behold, he drinketh; but he awaketh, and, behold, he is faint, and his soul hath appetite: so shall the multitude of all the nations be, that fight against mount Zion.

29.0.1.en: "Woe to Ariel, to Ariel, the city where David dwelt!" [1].

29.0.2.en: The word "Ariel" means "the fiery hearth of God," or "the lion of God," or "the mighty lion." It is a symbolic name meant for Jerusalem, as the city that contains in the Temple the altar of burnt offering blazing with fire (Ezek 43:15-16), and as the capital of the people of God, like the lion, the king of the beasts.

29.0.3.en: Ironside sees that Jerusalem was in former times like the lion of God, but she becomes more like a huge hearth for sacrifices, on which her people are offered at the hands of their bitter enemies.

29.0.4.en: King David, the prophet, used Ariel as his capital for a long time, and built his palace on Mount Zion, where the glory of God was afterwards declared in a wonderful way. His son Solomon built the Temple on Mount Moriah within Jerusalem, so the city became the center of communal worship, in which sacrifices were offered to the Lord, and she was counted as a lion in her spiritual strength. But when she became loosed from the spirit of true worship, was occupied with formalities without spirit, and was immersed in abominations with an insistence on not repenting, woe came upon her.

29.0.5.en: The people were accustomed to come to Jerusalem to celebrate three annual feasts [1], but God in His discipline turns these feasts into mourning and sorrow [2].

29.1.0.en: What does He mean by His saying, "and it shall be unto me as Ariel" [2]? Perhaps He wanted to declare that in her sorrow she becomes like a hearth of fire which God allowed to be kindled for the discipline of His wayward people; and perhaps He meant that although He allows her to be defeated and distressed, He makes her like a fiery altar for Himself, burning up the enemy who seized her, as a sacrifice to the Lord.

29.2.0.en: He expresses the measure of the sorrow that comes upon Jerusalem when she is besieged, saying: "And thou shalt be brought down, and shalt speak out of the ground, and thy speech shall be low out of the dust, and thy voice shall be as a phantom out of the ground, and thy speech shall whisper out of the dust" [4]. Because of her intense sorrow the inhabitants of Jerusalem sit in the dust like those at a "funeral," according to the ancient oriental traditions, and her voice comes out as if from the ground; and since they find none of the living to consult, they resort to the dead, seeking their counsel (Isa 8:19), and the voices come out faint, as if spiritual, and this is a kind of deception of the demons.

29.2.1.en: Yet in His love God intervenes suddenly with His lofty arm to save His city and His people from the army of Sennacherib (Isa 37:33-36), and the wrath of God falls upon the enemy, who scatters them like fine dust and like chaff in the blowing of the wind. He depicts this deliverance as a type of our salvation by the Cross and of the salvation of the Church at the end of the ages from the Antichrist:

29.3.0.en: A. The collapse of the enemy despite the greatness of his number and strength: "Moreover the multitude of thine enemies shall be like small dust, and the multitude of the terrible ones shall be as chaff that passeth away" [5]. These point to the devil and his angels, who are without number and fight humanity relentlessly, but before the Cross they become as nothing.

29.3.1.en: * We do not fear Satan even though he is a spirit without a body, for nothing is weaker than he who came to deal with us while being without a body, and no one is stronger than the brave man, even if he carries a body subject to death!

29.3.2.en: St. John Chrysostom B. The achievement of a swift victory: "yea, it shall be at an instant suddenly" [5], pointing to the surpassing power of the Cross to overcome enemies.

29.3.3.en: * With prayer, sign yourself with the Cross on your forehead, and then the demons will not come near you, because you will be armed against them.

29.4.0.en: St. John Chrysostom C. The Lord's salvation of this stricken city is accompanied by special signs in nature. "Thou shalt be visited of the LORD of hosts with thunder, and with earthquake, and great noise, with storm and tempest, and the flame of devouring fire" [6]. These signs point to what happened during the crucifixion of the Lord Christ, the upheaval of nature, such as the eclipse of the sun, the darkening of the moon, and the occurrence of an earthquake... and they also point to what will happen shortly before the final coming of the Lord Christ for judgment (Isa 28:21; 30:30; Zech 14:1-6; 2 Thess 1:6-8).

29.4.1.en: Perhaps the purpose of these signs is to rebuke man, whom God appointed lord of nature as the image and likeness of God, for lifeless nature bears witness to the saving works of God and condemns man's ingratitude and his disregard of his Creator and Savior.

29.5.0.en: D. The complete scattering of the enemies, for they vanish as in a dream of the night: when a man wakes, everything he saw disappears, and it is hard for him even to remember it [7].

29.6.0.en: The enemy who tried to seize the people of God will be like the hungry man who dreams that he eats, or the thirsty man who dreams that he drinks, only to wake and find himself as he was, hungry and thirsty [8].

29.7.s.en: 2. The spread of ignorance among His people:

29.7.0.en: 9 Be slothful and be astonished. Indulge yourselves and be blind. They are drunken, but not with wine; they stagger, but not with strong drink. 10 For the LORD hath poured out upon you the spirit of deep sleep, and hath closed your eyes: the prophets and your rulers, the seers hath he covered. 11 And the vision of all is become unto you as the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one that is learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I cannot; for it is sealed: 12 And the book is delivered to him that is not learned, saying, Read this, I pray thee: and he saith, I am not learned.

29.7.1.en: Besides the people's characteristic of covering an evil life with the formalities of worship, there was their ignorance of the word of God and their lack of experience of the power of the commandment in their lives.

29.7.2.en: If the Holy Spirit makes the soul drunk, giving it a heavenly joy that makes it forget the bitterness of affliction and pain, then spiritual ignorance makes it drunk by its drinking the cup of the wrath of God, and the fruit of this ignorance is:

29.7.3.en: A. Sloth [9]. The people grew slack and neglected the salvation of their souls, and became as if in a state of deep sleep [10], like sleepers who have lost spiritual feelings and holy sentiments, and watchfulness, and activity, and constant prayer, and the meeting with God in vitality.

29.7.4.en: St. John Chrysostom says: [The Apostle Paul, when he accused the people of falling into a state of deep sleep and lack of watchfulness (Rom 11:7-8)], resorted to the prophet David and Isaiah, lest this accusation be counted as coming from himself.

29.7.5.en: B. Being struck by a kind of dazzlement without enjoying the work of God. The truth shines before them like the sun, but their weak eyes deprived them of the enjoyment of its light, so they became dazzled by it without beholding it.

29.7.6.en: C. Delighting in a life of luxury [9].

29.8.0.en: D. The rejection of good counsel. There were prophets among them [10], as spiritual eyes by which the people, as well as the leaders, could behold the truth and understand the plan of God and His will. The prophets enjoyed visions, therefore they were called seers or beholders [10], but these visions remained a sealed book, either because what came in the book was obscure to them, or because of the people's inability to read it.

29.9.0.en: 13 Wherefore the Lord said, Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men: 14 Therefore, behold, I will proceed to do a marvellous work among this people, even a marvellous work and a wonder: for the wisdom of their wise men shall perish, and the understanding of their prudent men shall be hid.

29.9.1.en: Perhaps the most dangerous enemy that faces the religious is hypocrisy, or concern for formalities without the substance of the holy life. King Hezekiah began his reforms, but some abandoned the worship of idols outwardly and not from their heart; and they came to draw near to God with their lips and not their hearts, concerned with the praise of men and not of God, having a form of godliness while denying its power.

29.9.2.en: "Forasmuch as this people draw near me with their mouth, and with their lips do honour me, but have removed their heart far from me, and their fear toward me is taught by the precept of men" [13].

29.9.3.en: Origen links the people's drawing near to God with their lips without the heart to the spread of ignorance, that is, the claim of spiritual knowledge while not believing in the Lord Christ, and he says: [When the prophetic words become like the words of a sealed book, not only for those who do not know letters but for those who practice knowledge as a profession, then the Lord says that the people of the Jews draw near to the Lord only with their mouth and honour Him with their lips, because their heart is far from the Lord on account of their unbelief in Jesus].

29.9.4.en: St. Clement of Alexandria sees that God uncovered this fault not to take vengeance on them nor to expose them, but that they might realize their weaknesses and return to Him seeking their salvation. [Here His pastoral love made Him show their sins as He shows them salvation side by side].

29.9.5.en: From the comments of the Fathers on honoring God with the mouth without the heart:

29.9.6.en: * Many have understanding in their lips and not in their hearts.

29.9.7.en: * They drew near in body but stood far off in their hearts. Who was nearer to Him in body than those who lifted Him up on the Cross?! Who were farther from Him than those who blasphemed Him...? The very same persons who were near Him were also far from Him. They were near with their lips, far with their hearts.

29.9.8.en: St. Augustine * Let us cling to those who pledge peace by their godliness, not to those who profane the desire for godliness by hypocrisy.

29.9.9.en: * It is said: "They bless with their mouths, but their hearts curse" (Ps 63:4). And it is also said: "They loved him with their mouth, and lied unto him with their tongue; for their heart was not right with him, neither were they stedfast in his covenant"; "Let the lying lips be put to silence" (Ps 78:36-37; 31:8).

29.9.10.en: St. Clement of Rome * What does this mean? The true direction of the soul toward the truth is more precious than pleasing words in the sight of God, who hears the groanings which cannot be uttered.

29.9.11.en: A man can use expressions with an opposite meaning (to what they carry outwardly), for the tongue is ready to accomplish that according to the intention and purpose of the speaker, but the direction of the soul is seen by God, who knows the secrets.

29.10.s.en: 4. The third woe to him who trusts in his own wisdom:

29.10.0.en: 15 Woe unto them that seek deep to hide their counsel from the LORD, and their works are in the dark, and they say, Who seeth us? and who knoweth us? 16 Surely your turning of things upside down shall be esteemed as the potter's clay: for shall the work say of him that made it, He made me not? or shall the thing framed say of him that framed it, He had no understanding?

29.10.1.en: One of the signs of hypocrisy is that some of the nobles set in their hearts to carry out their own opinion, which was to resort secretly to Egypt against Assyria, in order to hide this matter not only from the people but even from God Himself, saying: "Who seeth us?! and who knoweth us?!" [15]. They thought, though they were the clay, that they were wiser than their Maker!

29.10.2.en: God, the Maker of man, in His humility wants to converse with man, the clay creature, while the creature in its pride thinks it is able to have knowledge with wisdom and understanding apart from its Maker, away from conversation with Him.

29.10.3.en: Father Martyrius the Syrian says: [How great is the grace of God's compassion and His condescension, which knows no limits! God comes down to the level of sinners, men and women; the good God speaks with rebellious servants; the Holy One calls the unclean to receive forgiveness. Humanity, created from clay, speaks with its Creator with boldness; the dust wages war against its Maker. Therefore let us show reverence when we, sinners, stand in the presence of this Great One and speak with Him].

29.11.0.en: 17 Is it not yet a very little while, and Lebanon shall be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field shall be esteemed as a forest? 18 And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity, and out of darkness. 19 The meek also shall increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel. 20 For the terrible one is brought to nought, and the scorner is consumed, and all that watch for iniquity are cut off: 21 That make a man an offender for a word, and lay a snare for him that reproveth in the gate, and turn aside the just for a thing of nought. 22 Therefore thus saith the LORD, who redeemed Abraham, concerning the house of Jacob, Jacob shall not now be ashamed, neither shall his face now wax pale. 23 But when he seeth his children, the work of mine hands, in the midst of him, they shall sanctify my name, and sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall fear the God of Israel. 24 They also that erred in spirit shall come to understanding, and they that murmured shall learn doctrine.

29.11.1.en: If the hidden, deceitful plans filled with hypocrisy bring distress and sorrow, then on the contrary the open saving work of God brings a succession of joys and countless blessings, among them:

29.11.2.en: A. A state of fruitfulness: "Is it not yet a very little while, and Lebanon shall be turned into a fruitful field, and the fruitful field shall be esteemed as a forest?" [17]. The open work of God turns Lebanon into a garden or a paradise; it turns the dry and rugged heart of man into the Kingdom of Christ, which bears the fruits of the Spirit; whereas man's deprivation of grace destroys even his natural fruits (the garden), so that it becomes rugged.

29.12.0.en: B. The gift of hearing the voice of God and seeing the divine mysteries: "And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity, and out of darkness" [18]. Spiritual hearing and inner insight are two gifts from God.

29.13.0.en: C. Enjoying the increasing inner heavenly joy: "The meek also shall increase their joy in the LORD, and the poor among men shall rejoice in the Holy One of Israel" [19].

29.14.0.en: D. The crushing of the enemy of good, the devil, and all his works, this tyrant who mocks the believers [20].

29.15.0.en: E. The nullifying of stumbling blocks and of all snares and evil counsels against the righteous children of God [21].

29.16.0.en: F. The removal of fear and shame: "Jacob shall not now be ashamed, neither shall his face now wax pale" [22].

29.17.0.en: G. The sanctification of the name of God: "But when he seeth his children (the children of Abraham), the work of mine hands, in the midst of him, they shall sanctify my name, and sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, and shall fear the God of Israel" [23]. It is as though the saying "Hallowed be Thy name" is fulfilled in them, since the name of God is sanctified in His people and His believers.

29.18.0.en: H. The change of human nature, so that they carry understanding and knowledge not in a purely rational manner but as a new life obedient to the Lord, after they had walked for a time in the error of ignorance and a life of rebellion and disobedience [24].

29.18.1.en: All these are the promises of God, which the Church of the New Testament enjoys, rejoicing in the joy of the Lord: her bearing the fruits of the Holy Spirit as the garden of Christ; her enjoyment of hearing the divine voice and seeing His divine mysteries instead of blindness; the crushing of the devil and all the powers of darkness; the overcoming of obstacles and stumbling blocks without fear or shame; and finally the sanctification of the name of God through spiritual understanding and obedience based on spiritual knowledge.
